'''Patrick Doreian''' is an American [[mathematician]] and [[social science|social scientist]], whose specialty is [[Social network analysis|network analysis]]. His specific research interests include [[blockmodeling]], [[social structure]] and [[network process]]es.<ref>[http://patrickdoreian.com/about/ Patrickdoreian.com - About Me]</ref>

Doreian, [[professor emeritus]] from the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in [[sociology]] and [[statistics]], was during his research career focused on social network research, especially regarding [[temporal network]]s, [[scientific collaboration]], [[partitioning network]]s, [[signed network]]s, [[network autocorrelation]] and the [[US Supreme Court]]. He was also an (co)editor of ''[[The Journal of Mathematical Sociology]]'' (1982–2005) and ''[[Social Networks (journal)|Social Networks]]'' (2006–2015).<ref>[https://www.fdv.uni-lj.si/en/news-and-information/news-and-notifications/professor-patrick-doreian-from-the-university-of-pittsburgh FDV.uni-lj.si - Professor Patrick Doreian from the University of Pittsburgh]</ref>

He was also a [[Centennial professor]] at the [[London School of Economics]] (2002) and a [[visiting professor]] at the [[University of California-Irvine]] and the [[University of Ljubljana]].<ref name="gener-black">{{Cite book |last1=Doreian |first1=Patrick |last2=Batagelj |first2=Vladimir |last3=Ferligoj |first3=Anuška |title=Generalized Blackmodeling |publisher=Cambridge University Press |date=2005 |isbn=0-521-84085-6}}</ref>

== Work ==
With [[Thomas J. Fararo]] in 1984, he introduced [[tripartite structural analysis]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fararo |first1=Thomas J |last2=Doreian |first2=Patrick |title=Tripartite structural analysis |journal=Social Networks |date=1984 |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=141–175|doi=10.1016/0378-8733(84)90015-7 }}</ref>

With [[Norman P. Hummon]] in 1989, he proposed a [[main path analysis]], a mathematical tool,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Hummon|first1=Norman P.|last2=Doreian|first2=Patrick|year=1989|title=Connectivity in a citation network: The development of DNA theory|journal=Social Networks|volume=11|issue=1|pages=39–63|doi=10.1016/0378-8733(89)90017-8}}</ref> to identify the major paths in a [[citation network]], which is one form of a [[directed acyclic graph]] (DAG).

In 1994, with [[Vladimir Batagelj]] and [[Anuška Ferligoj]], he introduced the [[generalized blockmodeling]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Žiberna |first1=Aleš |date=2009 |title=Evaluation of Direct and Indirect Blockmodeling of Regular Equivalence in Valued Networks by Simulations |url= |journal=Metodološki zvezki |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=99–134 |doi=}}</ref>

== Awards ==
His co-authored book ''Generalized blockmodeling'' (with [[Vladimir Batagelj]] and [[Anuška Ferligoj]]), was in 2007 awarded the Harrison White Outstanding Book Award by the Mathematical Sociology Section of [[American Sociological Association]].<ref name=bookaward>{{cite news|url=https://www.asanet.org/asa-communities/asa-sections/current-sections/mathematical-sociology/mathematical-sociology-section-award-recipients|title=The Section on Mathematical Sociology's Harrison White Outstanding Book Award|website=American Sociological Association|date=4 October 2011 |access-date=September 26, 2019}}</ref>

== Selected bibliography ==
* P. Doreian, [[Vladimir Batagelj|V. Batagelj]], [[Anuška Ferligoj|A. Ferligoj]], Mark Granovetter (Series Editor), ''Generalized Blockmodeling'' (Structural Analysis in the Social Sciences), Cambridge University Press 2004 ({{ISBN|0-521-84085-6}})
* P. Doreian and [[Andrej Mrvar|A. Mrvar]], “A Partitioning Approach to Structural Balance”, Social Networks, Vol. 18, 1996, pp.&nbsp;149–168
* P. Doreian and Andrej Mrvar (2009) “Partitioning Signed Social Networks”, Social Networks, Vol. 31: 1-11
* A. Mrvar and Patrick Doreian (2009), “Partitioning Signed Two-Mode Networks”, Journal of Mathematical Sociology, 33: 196-221
* A. Ferligoj, P. Doreian and V. Batagelj (2011): “Positions and Roles” Chapter 29 (pp 434–446) in [[John Scott (sociologist)|John Scott]] and [[Peter J. Carrington|Peter Carrington]] (Eds.) Handbook of Social Network Analysis, Newbury Park: Sage Publications
* P. Doreian, V. Batagelj and A. Ferligoj (2004), “Generalized Blockmodeling Two-Mode Network Data”, Social Networks, Vol. 26(1) 29-53.
